topics.accessibility: Accessibility options, readability, subtitles, colorblind support, difficulty options, or inclusive design features.
topics.audio: Music, sound effects, voice acting, soundtrack, audio quality, or sound design.
topics.bugs: Crashes, glitches, errors, broken quests, save issues, progression blockers, or technical malfunctions.
topics.content: Amount, variety, or depth of missions, stages, maps, characters, modes, items, activities, or things to do.
topics.controls: Keyboard, mouse, controller input, responsiveness, key mapping, camera control, or control comfort.
topics.difficulty_balance: Difficulty, fairness, enemy strength, progression curve, grind, balance, challenge, or frustration from tuning.
topics.gameplay: Core play experience, mechanics, combat, movement, interaction, game loop, moment-to-moment fun, or how the game plays.
topics.graphics: Visual quality, art style, animation, visual effects, character design, environment design, or overall look.
topics.monetization: DLC, microtransactions, paid content, gacha, pay-to-win, pricing model, or monetization structure.
topics.multiplayer: Online play, co-op, PvP, matchmaking, servers, connection quality, player base, or multiplayer community.
topics.other: Important review content that does not clearly fit any other allowed topic.
topics.performance: FPS, lag, stuttering, optimization, loading speed, crashes due to performance, hardware requirements, or technical smoothness.
topics.replayability: Replay value, repeated play, multiple endings, long-term motivation, roguelike loops, or reasons to return after finishing.
topics.story: Narrative, plot, characters, writing, dialogue, lore, worldbuilding, emotional storytelling, or campaign story.
topics.ui_ux: Menus, interface, HUD, readability, tutorials, navigation, usability, onboarding, or user experience outside direct controls.
topics.updates_support: Patches, developer support, updates, roadmap, maintenance, bug fixes after release, or post-launch support.
topics.value: Price, discount, worth the money, cost-benefit, whether the game is worth buying, or value for playtime.
topics.localization: Translation quality, language support, subtitles, text localization, voice localization, regional language issues, or problems caused by poor localization.
topics.network_server: Server stability, connection issues, disconnects, ping, latency, login problems, online service availability, or network-related technical issues.

distinction_rules: Use gameplay when the review discusses fun, mechanics, combat, movement, game loop, or how the game feels to play.
Use content when the review discusses amount of missions, maps, modes, items, stages, characters, or lack of things to do.
Use value when the review discusses price, discount, worth buying, value for money, or whether the game is worth the cost.
Use performance when the review discusses FPS, lag, optimization, loading, stuttering, or hardware-related smoothness.
Use bugs when the review discusses crashes, glitches, broken quests, errors, or progression blockers.
Use controls when the review discusses input, controller, keyboard, mouse, camera control, or responsiveness.
Use ui_ux when the review discusses menus, HUD, interface, readability, tutorials, navigation, or usability.
Use replayability when the review discusses playing again, long-term motivation, multiple endings, or repeated runs.
Use difficulty_balance when the review discusses fairness, challenge, grind, enemy strength, or balance.
A topic can appear in both positive_topics and negative_topics only when the review clearly praises and criticizes the same aspect.
Do not use a topic unless the review gives clear evidence for it.
Do not create new topics outside the allowed topic list.
Use localization when the review discusses translation, language support, subtitles, or poor localized text.
Use network_server when the review discusses server stability, connection problems, ping, latency, disconnects, or login/network issues.
Use multiplayer when the review discusses the design or experience of playing with other people; use network_server when the issue is technical connectivity or server reliability.
